isabella-montilla.desc: Paints Andean colours in a Montmartre studio and composes her attacks like a canvas.

ishita-rangoli.desc: Draws rangoli at the doorstep and builds pawn chains as symmetric and colorful as her patterns.

itzel-catrina.desc: Lights a candle for every captured piece and plays calm, haunting chess that rarely forgets a mistake.

ivy-lens.desc: Zooms in on one weak square and won’t stop looking at it.

jack-timber.desc: Climbs slowly and steadily. Patient in long manoeuvring games.

jaddah-latifa.desc: Hosts the whole family’s Eid gathering and plays with the same unhurried grace she pours gahwa.

jana-wald.desc: Explores every line, especially the long ones.

jaspal-gill.desc: Captures the moment your pieces line up for a skewer.

javi-montero.desc: Waves the red cape at your queen and steps aside at the very last second.

javiera-fuentes.desc: Twirls her skirt between moves and never lets a piece stand still for long.

jelena-kolo.desc: Dances the kolo at every wedding and spins her pieces in circles until something good happens.

jesse-field.desc: Brings a backpack full of opening tricks, all of them two moves long.

jhoan-escalona.desc: Star pitcher of his league in Osaka, and throws his pieces like fastballs down the middle.

jhonder-rangel.desc: Shoots weddings in San Salvador now and still frames every attack like a Caracas sunset.

jiwoo-seo.desc: Has read every opening book twice and plays like she already knows how the chapter ends.

joaqui-n-riquelme.desc: Dances the cueca with a handkerchief and circles your king the same way, step by step.

joey-pinstripe.desc: Reads your openings like a fastball, waits for the pitch he wants and swings hard.

johan-ceden-o.desc: Runs the busiest arepa truck in Miraflores and stuffs his positions just as full.

jonas-weber.desc: Every piece fits, every plan works.

joris.desc: Carries heavy pieces with a smile and sets them down exactly where they belong.

joy-adeyemi.desc: Chats nonstop and drops tactics mid-sentence.

juanse-ospina.desc: Keeps one foot on the ball and the other on the attack. Defense can wait.

julien-moreau.desc: Splashes color all over the board and calls the blunders impressionism.

juliette-chic.desc: Picks moves the way she picks handbags: whatever looks fabulous this season.

jun-jun.desc: Drives to the basket every move. Never passes, never stops smiling.

juninho-craque.desc: Dribbles every piece forward like he’s chasing a goal, and celebrates each capture with a little dance.

junior-vinotinto.desc: Wears the vinotinto with pride and runs at your king like a striker.

kai-keys.desc: Plays in tempo: every move gains time or it isn’t played.

kai-mahina.desc: Rides every attack like a wave and wipes out with a smile.

kaito-build.desc: AI, design, product, build, repeat. His preparation is relentless.

kalea-reef.desc: Dives deep into every line and surfaces with the truth.

katya-zima.desc: Cold outside, warm inside. Plays solid winter chess.

kavya-rang.desc: Plays Holi chess: colourful, joyful and all over the board.

kenia-portillo.desc: Makes heart hands at every opponent and gives away pieces just as generously.

kenji-byte.desc: Built his own chess engine and kind of plays like it.

kenji-mori.desc: Mixes quiet moves until the position reacts all at once.

keoni-uke.desc: Strums a happy tune and plays every move with aloha.

kevin-selva.desc: Moves as slowly as the sloths he rescues, and somehow still gets there first.

khalid-qahwa.desc: Pours the coffee three times and plays deep, generous chess.

kimo-poke.desc: Fresh, simple, perfectly balanced. Like a good poke bowl.

klodi-espresso.desc: Nurses one espresso for three hours by the water and plays just as slowly and smugly.

koa-nalu.desc: Waits for the perfect wave, then rides an attack all the way in.

kofi-kingsley.lose: You forked me first. Not fair!
kofi-kingsley.win: Fork! Did you see the fork?

kota-dango.desc: Eats hanami dango under the blossoms and grabs every piece in sight, one sweet bite at a time.

kuya-rolly.desc: Grew up watching the masters in the park. Plays fast, talks faster and almost never loses.

kwame-jr.desc: Just learned how the knight moves and uses it every single turn.

layla-amari.desc: Fights for every square, especially the ones nobody else wants.

leela.desc: Neural net that plays like a very strong human. Long plans, quiet sacrifices.

leif-trail.desc: Walks past volcanoes and blunders with the same calm.

lena-ridge.desc: Climbs the board with her pawns, one rank at a time.

leo-wander.win: The king’s journey was worth it.

leonardo-arismendi.desc: Writes backend code in Berlin and debugs every variation before he presses the clock.

liam-portage.desc: Treks through the Rockies all summer and takes the long scenic route to every checkmate.

linnea-berg.desc: Draws quietly in the corner and surprises you with a sharp tactic.

lotte.desc: Plants her pawns in neat rows and waits for the spring breakthrough.

lou-dubois.desc: Stops to snap a photo of every pretty position, even the ones she’s losing.

luana-costa.desc: Studies openings between lectures and plays like she already ran your moves through her laptop.

luca.desc: Glides his pieces down narrow canals you didn’t know were open.

lucho-pino.desc: Fills empanadas de pino at the fonda and packs every square with pressure before sealing the edge.

luci-a-disen-o.desc: Designs beautiful positions; function sometimes follows.

luci-a-marinera.desc: Courts your king with elegant moves, handkerchief in hand.

luci-a-mendes.desc: Hypothesis: your king is weak. Experiment: find out.

luisito-jonro-n.desc: Swings for the fences on every move. Home run or strikeout.

lukas-tor.desc: Efficient pressing, relentless counters, very little fuss.

luna-mochi.desc: Toys with your pieces like a cat with a ball of yarn.

luna-spin.desc: Keeps the moves flowing like a late-night playlist. Never a silent second.

makoa-ahi.desc: Patient as the ocean. Waits hours for a single tactic.

mama-juana.desc: Knows four thousand kinds of potato and just as many endgames.

mang-ben.desc: Knows every shortcut through the traffic. Picks up pawns along the route.

manon-leclerc.desc: Rushes out every morning for fresh bread and rushes her pieces out just as fast.

manuela-restrepo.desc: Studies in Medellín, carries her laptop everywhere and checks every line twice.

marco-calcio.desc: Dribbles past your defenders and celebrates every capture like a goal.

mariam-nasser.desc: Fuelled by iced qahwa and the positional squeeze.

marina-costa.desc: Spots danger fast and rescues pieces before they drown.

marisol-atlas.desc: Charts unusual routes for her knights. Every journey ends on an outpost.

marti-n-sur.desc: Treks Patagonia in any weather and plays in any position.

maryelis-guzma-n.desc: Spots eagles in the forests near Vancouver and keeps her binoculars on your queen.

master-huang-jun.desc: Trains at dawn and turns every attack you make back on you with soft, sudden blocks.

meera-iyer.desc: Design, build, ship: plans her pawn structure like a building.

milica-planina.desc: Climbs Kopaonik on weekends and grinds through long games one careful step at a time.

milos-barjak.desc: Carries the flag at every parade and marches his pawns forward with the same proud, steady stride.

minjun-kang.desc: Bows politely, then attacks the kingside with the same snap as his front kick.

minjun-yut.desc: Throws yut sticks with a yell and moves pieces wherever the throw feels lucky.

mio-ink.desc: Inks bold lines across the board, then fills in the details.

misha-lyzhi.desc: Races downhill toward your king with no brakes.

nia-sugar.desc: Takes every pawn offered, like free cookies.

nils-kod.desc: Ships apps from Stockholm and plays clean, tested chess with zero unnecessary lines.

noah-script.desc: Plays by checklist: checks, captures, threats. Usually remembers all three.

noura-henna.desc: Draws henna the night before Eid and weaves her pieces into delicate, connected nets.

ole-laks.desc: Never lets a free salmon, or a free pawn, get away.

olena-knyha.desc: History, design, tech, and old-school chess precision.

olive-hayes.desc: Grows her pawns into a long chain, then forgets about her king.

ollie-peak.desc: Explores every corner of the board, especially the edges.

oriana-castillo.desc: Runs on iced coffee in the Maracaibo heat and plays blitz on the bus home with a proud maracucho accent.

oscar-penn.desc: Solves puzzles all day and sees combinations that aren’t quite there.

oskar-svensson.desc: Assembles positions like flat-pack furniture: step by step, no pieces left over.

owen-shutter.desc: Replays his favourite blunders in slow motion.

pablito-gol.desc: Wears the number 10 and runs every piece straight at goal, defense optional.

paco-molina.desc: Plucks quiet little moves for an hour, then strums a mating attack nobody saw coming.

paloma-sol.desc: Packs light: trades pieces early and travels into the endgame.

paolo.desc: Casts a wide net across the board and waits for something to bite.

papa-andre-s.desc: Plays one-handed, baby in the other arm. Surprisingly calm.

papa-ge-rard.desc: Has played the same café table for forty years and knows every trap by its vintage.

paquito-calaca.desc: Decorates sugar skulls with way too much icing and covers the board in bright, messy attacks.

paz-calma.desc: Strong core, steady centre. Never makes a jerky move.

pepe-payaso.desc: Juggles three plans at once and drops at least two.

pepito-serenata.desc: Only knows three chords and two openings, and he plays both with his whole heart.

per-olof-sill.desc: Leads every snapsvisa at the long table and strikes in tempo with the last line of the song.

peyton-spirit.lose: Great game! Two, four, six, eight!

pip-pawnworth.lose: Okay, okay, I see it now. Rematch!

pip-volta.desc: Every move is an experiment, and most of them fizz over.

pixel.desc: Speedruns the opening and plays the middlegame like a boss fight.

poppy-lane.desc: Loves castling so much she has tried to do it twice.

prakash-mithai.hello: Have a ladoo first, then we play.

priya-pages.desc: Studies your last move for a long time and usually finds the right answer.

priya-solder.desc: Connects her pieces like a circuit. Cut one wire and the rest still work.

profe-ana.desc: Ideas, plan, discipline, freedom: she teaches all four in one game.

professor-albrecht.desc: Sees the whole board as one beautiful equation, and solves it.

professor-fizz.desc: Experiments with odd sidelines just to see what reacts.

professor-idris.desc: Lectures you with every move. The lecture is, unfortunately, correct.

rafael-lima.desc: Counter-attacks like a striker: waits back, then sprints.

rania-lens.desc: Chases golden-hour light and loose pieces.

ravi-grand.desc: Makes your pieces disappear. Look closely at his last move.

ray-mendoza.desc: Knows every shortcut in the city at 3 a.m. Gets your king home the fast way.

remy-static.desc: Bullet habits: moves first, thinks later.

ren-ono.desc: Wanders Tokyo with a camera and wanders the board the same way.

rescue-rory.desc: Spends the whole game guarding his king and rescuing pieces in danger.

rico-cool.desc: Too cool to calculate. Plays on vibes.

rina-flash.desc: Snaps fast moves and checks them later. Sometimes too late.

roci-o-vargas.desc: Stamps out sharp tactics to a fierce rhythm and finishes every combination with a flourish.

rodrigo-quintanilla.desc: Leads hikes up Cerro Verde and Santa Ana and always knows the safe path to the top.

sage-rivers.hello: A game is a poem in sixty-four squares.

saif-eidiya.desc: Collects eidiya from every uncle and spends his pieces just as fast as his coins.

sakura-ito.desc: Each move as deliberate as a tea ceremony. Not a gesture wasted.

salim-muscat.desc: Easy-going and careful; never makes the same mistake twice.

sam-biscuit.desc: Sam plays, Biscuit supervises. Neither of them likes long endgames.
sam-biscuit.lose: Biscuit is proud of you anyway.

sammy-stripes.desc: Points at your king on move one and waves a flag at every capture, win or lose.
sammy-stripes.hello: I want YOU to play me!

sangwoo-baek.desc: Mixes every piece into the center like a good bibimbap and trusts it all to taste right.

sasha-balalaika.desc: Three strings, three moves of plan. Plays for fun.

sasha-print.desc: Prints her pieces layer by layer. Slow start, solid finish.

selene-silk.desc: Balances on a knife edge and somehow never falls.

sem.desc: Pedals his pieces everywhere, ringing the bell at every check.

seo-yeon-yoon.desc: Opens her fan, then her position, one graceful fold at a time until you run out of squares.

seoyeon-yeon.desc: Flies her kite over the frozen river and keeps her long-range pieces soaring on open diagonals.
seoyeon-yeon.hello: Saehae bok! Watch my kite fly.

sepp-huber.desc: Built like the Alps: slow to move, impossible to push over.

sf11.desc: The pre-neural version. Materialistic, brutal in tactics, beatable positionally.

sf18.desc: Current release with a level cap. Clean strength test, no personality, no commentary.

signora-lucia.desc: Rolls out long, patient plans by hand. No shortcuts in her kitchen.

simo-n-cuatro.desc: Plays to a joropo rhythm: quick, quick, then a sudden flourish.

simone-vale.desc: Makes decisions fast and never second-guesses a good trade.
simone-vale.hello: I have ten minutes. Make them count.

sixten-groda.desc: Hops like a little frog around the maypole and leaps his pieces all over the board.
sixten-groda.win: Kou ack ack ack! I won!

sofi-mate.desc: Shares her mate, shares nothing on the board. Slow and sweet.
sofi-mate.win: Another round of mate to celebrate.

sofia-reyes.desc: Prepares your favourite opening before the game. Spooky.
sofia-reyes.lose: You surprised me. I like that.

solveig-fjord.desc: Cross-country stamina: she will happily play eighty moves.
solveig-fjord.lose: You were faster on the downhill.

sonya-bilyk.desc: Ideas, build, better tomorrows: optimistic and endlessly resourceful.

sophie-leblanc.desc: Has read every opening book in the library and shushes your attack with quiet, tidy defense.

sora-tanaka.desc: Counts every exchange. If the numbers say trade, he trades.

stefan-tamburas.desc: Strums the tamburica between moves and keeps a happy rhythm even when his position is falling apart.

stella-shade.desc: Plays coolly, never shows emotion, never shows her plan.

su-wenqing.desc: Forty years of brushstrokes taught her that every stroke counts. Never a wasted move.

sunny-park.desc: Every position is great, even the lost ones.
sunny-park.hello: Today feels like a winning day!
sunny-park.lose: Still a great day. Well played!

taeyang-oh.desc: Climbs toward your king one slow, steady step at a time, poles first, never in a hurry.

tante-mies.desc: Has played at the same chess café for sixty years. Coffee, cake and a quiet sacrifice.

taras-sokil.desc: Wears his vyshyvanka with pride and fights for every square.

tariq-rimal.desc: Crosses Wadi Rum on foot, and the board the same way: steadily.

tasha-wells.desc: Likes closed positions and symmetrical pawns. Very happy with a draw.

tatev.desc: Knots her pieces into intricate patterns. Every corner of the board is part of the design.

tempo-tarik.desc: Moves in under two seconds and punishes every slow developing move you make.

thai-s-frevo.desc: Dances frevo through Olinda with a tiny umbrella and balances wild tactics on one foot.

thai-s-mendonc-a.desc: Keeps her pieces moving to a samba beat and loves a flashy sacrifice right before the big finish.
thai-s-mendonc-a.lose: Ai, you stepped on my toes. Nice!

the-archivist.desc: Twenty moves of theory in every main line, then plays like a strong club player.
the-archivist.lose: A new entry for the archive.

theo-bones.desc: Digs up old openings nobody plays anymore and dusts them off.

ti-a-carmen.desc: Feeds you tequeños and then takes all your pieces. With love.

ti-a-nelly-hallaca.desc: Ties two hundred hallacas every December and wraps up loose positions just as tightly.
ti-a-nelly-hallaca.hello: Ven, help me tie the hallacas.

tiago-swell.desc: Rides the momentum: once he is attacking, he never lets the wave break.
tiago-swell.win: Rode that one all the way in.

tilda-jordgubbe.desc: Picks the reddest strawberries for the tårta and collects loose pawns just as carefully.

tina-sprocket.desc: Builds plans out of spare parts. Some of them even work.

tita-marites.desc: Waits for every advantage to ripen, then harvests it all at once.

toby-bright.desc: Does not mind losing pieces as long as the game is fun.

toby-hops.desc: Bounces his pieces around without stopping. Lots of energy, little plan.

toma-s-hotus.desc: Sits with the moai every evening and plays as calmly as a statue that has seen it all.

toma-s-salgado.desc: Haggles over every pawn and always gets a fair price.

tomasito-trompo.desc: Spins his trompo at the fonda and lets pieces whirl around until something falls.

tomi-ideas.desc: Pivots plans mid-game and somehow lands on a good one.
tomi-ideas.hello: Got a good idea for this.

tommy-tactics.desc: Sets one-move traps and waits. Sometimes you walk right in.
tommy-tactics.hello: Nothing to see here. Totally normal moves.
tommy-tactics.lose: You saw it coming, didn’t you?

toni-socarrat.desc: Never stirs the pan and never rushes the endgame. The good part is at the bottom.

tonico-viola-o.desc: Plays slow and smooth like a bossa nova chord, never hurrying, always finding the right note.
tonico-viola-o.lose: Beautiful melody. You win this one.
tonico-viola-o.win: Saudade for your king, meu amigo.

tove-backlund.desc: Races down the slopes of Åre and plays fast, downhill chess that only brakes for checkmate.

uncle-ray.desc: Old school: the Ruy Lopez, the Queen’s Gambit, and a long think before every capture.
uncle-ray.hello: In my day we played the Ruy Lopez.

usta-hakan.desc: Shaves material off your position slice by slice and keeps the fire roaring the whole game.
usta-hakan.lose: Ah, you burned me. Again, abi?

v2023_06.desc: Four moves of theory, then pure improvisation. Leaves pieces where they land.

v2024_02.desc: Takes every trade on offer and simplifies straight out of good positions.

v2025_01.desc: Sacrifices on h7 without counting defenders. Sharp, fast, occasionally brilliant.

v2026_09.desc: Your current habits mirrored back. Solid until the clock drops under a minute.

valen.desc: Plays like she studies: organised, caffeinated, a little stressed.

valentina-ochoa.desc: Designs warm houses in a cold city, and builds positions the same way: brick by brick.
valentina-ochoa.hello: God dag, chama. Shall we build?

valeria-andes.desc: Picks the safest route up the mountain and never rushes the summit.

valeria-code.desc: Writes clean code and cleaner endgames. The capybara sticker is her lucky charm.

varpet-hovik.desc: Carves positions that stand for centuries. Every move cut with care.

vic-ash.desc: Plays sharp lines at 2 a.m. and somehow doesn’t blunder.

vika-volk.desc: Hunts like a wolf: circles, waits, then strikes.

vikram-shanti.desc: Mind, discipline, peace. Never hurries, never errs.

vilgot-tomte.desc: Dresses as a little tomte and sneaks pieces around the board hoping nobody notices.
vilgot-tomte.hello: God jul! I’m a tomte today.
vilgot-tomte.win: The tomte got you! Ho ho!

wei-longfei.desc: Spreads his attack like a dragon fan: one flick and the whole flank opens.

willow-hart.desc: Plants pawns and waits to see what grows.
willow-hart.hello: Patience is a gardener’s best tool.

xiao-yu.desc: Collects panda everything and cheers every capture, even yours.

ximena-cempasu-chil.desc: Lays marigold petal paths to the altar and guides her pieces down open files the same way.
ximena-cempasu-chil.kind: marigold path keeper · Día de Muertos
ximena-cempasu-chil.lose: You found the path first. Bravo.

xiomara-rivas.desc: Dances the xuc in a blue and white skirt and spins her pieces into tidy, graceful patterns.

yami-pollera.desc: Twirls through the centre in her pollera, every step practised for years.

yasmin-dhahab.desc: Every move polished like gold. Rarely, if ever, a flaw.

yeferson-lugo.desc: Top scorer of his youth team in São Paulo, and chases every attack like a through ball.

yelitza-carrasquel.desc: Runs a busy arepera in Lavapiés and serves up tactics as hot as her arepas.
yelitza-carrasquel.kind: arepera owner · Puerto La Cruz → Madrid

yhonny-ma-rquez.desc: Swapped Maracaibo heat for Moscow snow. Plays warm, sharp gambits to keep his hands busy.
yhonny-ma-rquez.hello: Brrr, chamo. Let’s heat this board up.
yhonny-ma-rquez.lose: Too cold to think. Rematch, pana.

yolanda-palacios.desc: Sells fruit from a basket in Cartagena and knows every piece’s value to the last peso.

yolimar-cafe.desc: Strong guayoyo, strong centre. Wakes up around move twelve and starts attacking.

yui-neko.desc: Plays dramatic sacrifices straight out of her favourite manga.

yuleisy-pe-rez.desc: Coaches the best youth baseball team in Manila. Calls every play like a pitch count.

yuliana-caicedo.desc: Swirls a skirt in yellow, blue and red and moves her pieces with the same flair.
yuliana-caicedo.lose: Ay, I lost the step. Otra.

yuna-ryu.desc: Every move is a stage moment: flashy, confident, and followed by a wink whether it works or not.

yusmary-colmenares.desc: Runs the night shift at a Santiago hospital and checks every piece like vital signs.

yusmary-furruco.desc: Keeps the gaita rhythm on her furruco and plays steady chess that never skips a beat.

zara-twirl.desc: Spins her pieces gracefully around the centre. Light on her feet.

zeke-kickflip.desc: Flips the balance with wild pawn sacrifices. Lands about half of them.

zhou-lan.desc: Hikes the Great Wall with a camera and wanders the board looking for the perfect shot.

zolta-n-husza-r.desc: Leads cavalry charges across the board with sabre drawn and moustache perfectly waxed.
zolta-n-husza-r.lose: A worthy foe. Le a kalappal!

zso-fi-koboz.desc: Strums old folk tunes and plays dreamy, flowing moves with her eyes half closed.
zso-fi-koboz.hello: Szia! A song for the opening?

zugzwang-zoya.desc: Trades into the ending at the first chance and squeezes from there.
zugzwang-zoya.hello: Let’s skip to the good part: the endgame.
zugzwang-zoya.win: Any move you make is worse. Zugzwang.

zuri-bello.desc: Brings everything to the kingside and laughs when it works.
zuri-bello.hello: Your king looks lonely over there.
zuri-bello.win: Ha! Told you it would work!

bird.idea: White grabs e5 with the f-pawn, like a Dutch Defense with an extra move. The king is a little looser, so watch the e1–h4 diagonal.
bird.name: Bird's Opening
bird.origin: Named after Henry Bird, an English master who kept playing it in the 19th century when almost nobody else did.

caro-kann.idea: Like the French, Black prepares …d5, but with the c-pawn, so the light-squared bishop can still come out. Solid and hard to crack.
caro-kann.name: Caro-Kann Defense
caro-kann.origin: Named after Horatio Caro and Marcus Kann, who analysed it together in the 1880s.

colle.idea: A quiet setup with the bishop on d3 and the knight on d2, aiming for the e3–e4 break that opens lines toward the black king.
colle.name: Colle System
colle.origin: Named after Edgar Colle, a Belgian master of the 1920s who built his repertoire around it.

dutch.idea: Black fights for e4 with the f-pawn and often attacks on the kingside, at the price of a slightly looser king.
dutch.name: Dutch Defense
dutch.origin: Named after the Dutch player Elias Stein, who recommended it in a book at the end of the 18th century.

english.idea: White controls d5 from the side and keeps flexible: the game can turn into a reversed Sicilian or transpose into a 1.d4 opening.
english.name: English Opening
english.origin: Named after the English champion Howard Staunton, who played it in his famous 1843 match against Saint-Amant.

french.idea: Black prepares …d5 to challenge e4. The position is solid but the light-squared bishop is often stuck behind the e6 pawn.
french.name: French Defense
french.origin: Named after a correspondence match between London and Paris in the 1830s, where the Paris team used it.

italian.idea: The bishop aims at f7, the weakest square next to the black king. Develop fast, castle, and prepare d4.
italian.name: Italian Game
italian.origin: Named after the Italian masters of the 16th and 17th centuries, like Gioachino Greco, who analysed it. Its quiet main line is called the Giuoco Piano, "the quiet game".

kings-gambit.idea: White offers the f-pawn to tear open the f-file and the center, accepting risk to the king for a fast attack.
kings-gambit.name: King's Gambit
kings-gambit.origin: The favourite of the romantic era of the 19th century, when sacrifices and attack ruled the board.

kings-indian.idea: Black lets White build a big center, then attacks it, often with …e5 and a pawn storm on the kingside.
kings-indian.name: King's Indian Defense
kings-indian.origin: The "Indian" defences take their name from the 19th-century Indian player Moheschunder Bannerjee, who played fianchetto setups like this one. It became a top-level weapon in the mid-20th century.

kings-knight.idea: White develops and attacks the e5 pawn in one move. The Italian, the Ruy Lopez, the Scotch and the Philidor all begin from this position.
kings-knight.name: King's Knight Opening
kings-knight.origin: Named for the knight that develops with tempo against e5. Most of the classic open games start here.

kings-pawn.idea: One move opens lines for the queen and the light-squared bishop and grabs the center. Expect open, tactical games.
kings-pawn.name: King's Pawn Game
kings-pawn.origin: Named for the pawn in front of the king, the most popular first move in chess history.

london.idea: A system more than a line: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3 and Bd3 against almost anything. The bishop comes out before e3 locks it in.
london.name: London System
london.origin: Named after the London tournament of 1922, where several masters used the setup.

philidor.idea: Black holds e5 with a pawn instead of a piece: solid, a little cramped, with the bishop on e7 and the c-pawn ready to support d5 later.
philidor.name: Philidor Defense
philidor.origin: Named after François-André Danican Philidor, the strongest player of the 18th century and also a celebrated opera composer.

pirc.idea: Black lets White take the center, fianchettoes the bishop on g7, and strikes at the center later.
pirc.name: Pirc Defense
pirc.origin: Named after Vasja Pirc, a Slovenian grandmaster of the 20th century. Its close cousin, 1…g6, is called the Modern Defense.

queens-gambit.idea: White offers the c-pawn to pull Black’s d-pawn away from the center. It is not a real gambit: White can almost always win the pawn back.
queens-gambit.name: Queen's Gambit
queens-gambit.origin: One of the oldest openings on record, analysed since the early days of modern chess.

queens-pawn.idea: The d4 pawn is protected by the queen from the start, so White claims the center without giving a target. Games tend to be slower and more strategic than after 1.e4.
queens-pawn.name: Queen's Pawn Game
queens-pawn.origin: Named for the pawn in front of the queen. Every opening that starts 1.d4 grows from it.

ruy-lopez.idea: The bishop attacks the knight that defends e5. The pressure lasts for many moves, which is why it has been a favourite of world champions for over a century.
ruy-lopez.name: Ruy Lopez
ruy-lopez.origin: Named after Ruy López de Segura, a Spanish priest who wrote about it in a chess book in 1561. Also called the Spanish Game.

scandinavian.idea: Black challenges e4 at once. After 2.exd5 Qxd5 the queen comes out early, so Black must be ready to move it again.
scandinavian.name: Scandinavian Defense
scandinavian.origin: Named after Scandinavian players who analysed it in the 19th century. Often cited as the opening of the oldest recorded chess game, from Valencia in 1475.

scotch.idea: White opens the center at once instead of building slowly. The pieces get free play, and Black must react accurately.
scotch.name: Scotch Game
scotch.origin: Named after a correspondence match between Edinburgh and London in 1824, where the Edinburgh team played it.

sicilian.idea: Black fights for d4 from the side, creating an unbalanced game. It is the most popular reply to 1.e4 at master level, and the sharpest.
sicilian.name: Sicilian Defense
sicilian.origin: Described by Italian authors as early as the late 1500s, and named after players from Sicily.

slav.idea: Black defends d5 with the c-pawn instead of the e-pawn, so the light-squared bishop can still come out to f5 or g4.
slav.name: Slav Defense
slav.origin: Named after the many Slavic masters who developed it in the early 20th century.

trompowsky.idea: The bishop goes straight to g5 to pin or trade off the f6 knight before Black settles into a familiar setup.
trompowsky.name: Trompowsky Attack
trompowsky.origin: Named after the Brazilian master Octávio Trompowsky, who played it in the middle of the 20th century.

uncommon.idea: They avoid theory, but usually give the opponent the center for free. Answer them with simple development: take the center, bring out the pieces, castle.
uncommon.name: Uncommon Openings
uncommon.origin: A catch-all for first moves outside the main openings. Some have colorful names of their own, but none is common at master level.

vienna.idea: White develops the queen’s knight first, keeping the option of f4 later, like a King’s Gambit with better preparation.
vienna.name: Vienna Game
vienna.origin: Named after the Vienna players who developed it in the middle of the 19th century.
